facts.statement: Alamitornis is classified as an extinct genus of basal ornithuromorph dinosaurs that may belong to the family Patagopterygidae.
facts.quote: Alamitornis is an extinct genus of basal ornithuromorph dinosaurs, possibly within the family Patagopterygidae.

facts.statement: The genus was first named by Federico L. Agnolin and Agustín G. Martinelli in 2009, with the type species being Alamitornis minutus.
facts.quote: It was first named by Federico L. Agnolin and Agustín G. Martinelli in 2009 and the type species is Alamitornis minutus.

facts.statement: Fossils of Alamitornis were found in the Upper Cretaceous Los Alamitos Formation in the Río Negro Province of Argentina.
facts.quote: Remains have been found in the Upper Cretaceous Los Alamitos Formation at Los Alamitos, Río Negro Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Alamitornis is placed in the unranked order Patagopterygiformes.
Alamitornis lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Alamitornis is Ornithothoraces.
